title: Japanese for the Pharmacy in 9 Comic Scenes | Guess, Listen, Say It (Travel Japanese)
lead: Caught a cold on your trip? Describe your symptoms and buy medicine at a Japanese pharmacy, in nine comic scenes. Guess first, then listen twice and say it.

intro.title:
Japan pharmacy
**9 phrases**
intro.say: Nine scenes in a Japanese pharmacy. Guess each line before the answer.

phrases.label: Cold medicine
phrases.when: Looking for cold medicine? Ask like this.
phrases.tip: Kaze is a cold and kusuri is medicine. Tell the staff your symptoms and let them help you choose.
phrases.scene: At the pharmacy counter, Jiwoo wears a white face mask pulled down under her chin and sniffles, asking the pharmacist behind the counter; Minjun stands behind her holding a tissue box.

phrases.label: I have a fever
phrases.when: When they ask what is wrong, say this if you have a fever.
phrases.tip: If the fever is high or lasts for days, see a doctor rather than relying on medicine.
phrases.hear: どうされましたか？ (Dou saremashita ka?) = What seems to be the problem?
phrases.scene: At the counter, the pharmacist asks with a concerned look; Jiwoo touches her forehead with the back of her hand, cheeks a little flushed.

phrases.label: Sore throat
phrases.when: If your throat hurts, say this.
phrases.tip: Itai desu means it hurts. Head is atama, stomach is onaka: atama ga itai desu.
phrases.scene: At the counter, Jiwoo gently touches her throat with a pained little face; the pharmacist nods and listens carefully.

phrases.label: Allergies
phrases.ja: アレルギーはありません。
phrases.when: The pharmacist asks if you have allergies. If not, answer like this.
phrases.tip: If you do have one, write it in Japanese on your phone beforehand and show it.
phrases.hear: アレルギーはありますか？ (Arerugii wa arimasu ka?) = Do you have any allergies?
phrases.scene: The pharmacist holds a small plain medicine box and asks a question; Jiwoo shakes her head lightly with a reassuring hand gesture.

phrases.label: Will it make me sleepy?
phrases.ja: この薬は眠くなりますか？
phrases.pron: Kono kusuri wa nemuku narimasu ka?
phrases.ko: Does this medicine make you drowsy?
phrases.when: Want to know if it causes drowsiness? Ask this.
phrases.tip: Many cold and travel-sickness medicines can make you sleepy. Always ask if you plan to drive.
phrases.scene: Jiwoo holds the small plain medicine box and mimes a sleepy face with her head resting on her hands; the pharmacist smiles and answers.

phrases.label: How often
phrases.ja: 一日何回飲めばいいですか？
phrases.pron: Ichinichi nankai nomeba ii desu ka?
phrases.ko: How many times a day should I take it?
phrases.when: Ask how many times a day to take it like this.
phrases.tip: After meals is shokugo, before meals is shokuzen.
phrases.scene: Jiwoo holds up the medicine box and counts on her fingers with a questioning look; the pharmacist holds up three fingers.

phrases.label: Travel-sickness pills
phrases.ja: 酔い止めはありますか？
phrases.ko: Do you have anything for motion sickness?
phrases.when: Need something before a boat or bus ride? Ask this.
phrases.tip: Most motion-sickness medicine is taken before you travel.
phrases.scene: Jiwoo points at Minjun, who looks pale and holds his stomach, and asks the pharmacist, who reaches for a small box on the shelf behind her.

phrases.label: Plasters
phrases.when: Got a small cut? Ask for bandages like this.
phrases.tip: Bansoukou means adhesive bandages. Convenience stores sell them too.
phrases.scene: Minjun holds up one finger with a tiny cut; Jiwoo points at it and asks the pharmacist, who holds out a small plain box of adhesive bandages.

bonus.label: Finding a clinic
bonus.ja: 近くに病院はありますか？
bonus.pron: Chikaku ni byouin wa arimasu ka?
bonus.ko: Is there a hospital or clinic nearby?
bonus.when: Finally, if medicine is not enough, ask for a doctor nearby like this.
bonus.scene: Jiwoo, looking a little worried, asks the pharmacist, who points toward the store door with an open hand and a reassuring smile; Minjun holds the shopping bag.

outro.title: Recap: **9 phrases**
outro.say: All the phrases are in the description. Tell us in the comments how many you got right. Subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
